notes: Check batch 2026-11-05-check-4: four skill runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus run, all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier (each transcript's assistant messages name only that tier's model). All four ran at head b897c24 with uncommitted true and one skill_hash (ad261b76...); skills_listed 62. Every transcript contains the new `->` heading text ("unless the clauses read as a table", "A row that calls on") and the other working-tree sentences ("whose failure already has the shape", "may return `nil`, as a `get` does", "Different failures need different reasons"), so the runs read the current text. Reads: SKILL.md only in haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1; SKILL.md and library-design.md in sonnet-2. Expected reads is none beyond SKILL.md, so all four meet it, as earlier sweeps counted extra reads. In the scratch folder all four files pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.3). Doctests: haiku-1 none, haiku-2 1 of 1, sonnet-1 3 of 3, sonnet-2 3 of 3.

Changed rules: git diff 74112b4 -- idiomatic-elixir/ (commits since 74112b4 plus the uncommitted working tree the runs read) changes four of the ten graded rules. The `->` rule is renamed from "Inline `->` clauses that read at a glance; otherwise put each body on its own line" to "Put each `->` body on its own line unless the clauses read as a table" and graded under the new heading. Its deciding sentences are now "A clause of `case`, `cond`, `receive`, `with ... else` or a multi-clause `fn` puts its body on the line after the `->`. The exception is clauses that read as a table" and "A row that calls on, as `{:ok, bytes} -> hash_if_canonical(token, bytes)` does beside `_other -> :error`, does not read that way, because one row gives an answer and the other hands off"; the second decides haiku-2 lines 139-140 violated, the first holds the returning tables of haiku-1 and haiku-2 clean, and the 70-character limit ("A table row past about 70 characters after the indentation still breaks") holds the two 70-character rows clean, as 2026-10-31-b and 2026-11-05-check-3 held 70. Match every expected shape adds "Different failures need different reasons too" and the nil-lookup exception; it decides nothing: all four runs return :invalid_payload, {:unsupported_event, type}, {:missing_field, key} and {:invalid_field, key} as distinct reasons (verified), and both Sonnet runs are violated under the unchanged catch-all text. Chain fallible steps adds "Give each step a private function whose failure already has the shape the function holding the `with` returns", the value-or-nil guard step, the "An `else` whose every clause returns the same value is the sign" sentence and "when that call does not return `{:ok, value}`, the `case` goes in a small private function"; none decides anything, since every step is a private function returning {:ok, _} or {:error, _} inside a function that returns tuples, no with has an else, and no case is nested in a with body. The return-tuple rule adds "A lookup whose only failure is absence may return `nil`"; no run writes such a lookup. All other verdicts are held to the 2026-10-31-b standard.

Inline `->` clauses (every case, cond, receive or with ... else whose clauses sit on one line): haiku-1 occurred_at/1 lines 93-96 (both rows return a tuple: table, clean); haiku-1 string_field/2 lines 143-147 (three rows each return a tuple: table, clean); haiku-1 amount_field/2 lines 151-155 (three returning rows, line 152 exactly 70 characters after the indentation: table, clean); haiku-1 optional_string_field/2 lines 159-162 (two returning rows: table, clean); haiku-2 occurred_at/1 lines 99-102 (both rows return a tuple: table, clean); haiku-2 string_field/2 lines 138-141 (line 139 {:ok, value} -> text(value, key) calls on beside line 140 :error -> {:error, {:missing_field, key}}, which returns: not a table, violated); haiku-2 amount_field/1 lines 145-149 (three returning rows, line 146 exactly 70: table, clean). sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 have no inline -> clause: every case clause has its body on the next line with blank lines between. No run writes a cond, receive, with ... else or multi-clause fn.

Closest calls. Match every expected shape: sonnet-1 line 141 defp parse_data(_payment_type, data) do and sonnet-2 line 145 defp parse_data(_payment_type, %{} = data) do are the payment catch-all 2026-10-31 graded violated in skill-sonnet-1 and 2026-11-05-check and -check-3 in skill-sonnet-2. sonnet-1 line 129 _invalid -> {:error, {:invalid_field, "created"}} after {:ok, created_at} receives only the false of a non-integer created or DateTime.from_unix/1's {:error, _}, both an invalid created, so it is not counted, as 2026-10-22-c did not count baseline-opus-1's _other clause in fetch_timestamp/2's else; counted, it would not change the verdict. haiku-2 line 111 and sonnet-2 line 163 (a parse_data/payload clause for non-map data) receive only a known kind with non-map data, which their error names, held clean as 2026-11-05-check held haiku-2's line 112. The non-string type reaching {:unsupported_event, 123} in all four runs is kept in checks, as 2026-10-31-b and both earlier 2026-11-05 batches did. Read required keys: haiku-1's Map.get (line 159) and haiku-2's data["failure_reason"] (line 123) read fields the structs leave out of @enforce_keys, so optional. Multi-clause: haiku-1's event_data/2, haiku-2's payload/2 and the Sonnet parse_data/2 take data as a positional argument (sonnet-2 with a %{} = data alias), not a field bound from a matched value. Naming: haiku-1's object and raw_type, haiku-2's kind, payload and text/2, sonnet-2's map and non_empty_string/2 not counted, as kind, payload and object were before. Structs: haiku-1's three payload structs are @moduledoc false, not counted, as 2026-10-31 did not count haiku-2's. Outside the list: sonnet-1 line 125 case is_integer(created) and DateTime.from_unix(created) do uses and to pick a value, its right operand a result tuple; decided not counted under "Use `and`, `or`, `not` when the operands are booleans", because the rule's body sets and against && by the operand and checks ("raise if their first operand is not a boolean"), and that operand is is_integer/1's boolean, so && would be the weaker choice here; no earlier grade met this shape, and counted it would sit in sonnet-1's other_violations only; sonnet-1's {:ok, / %Payment{...}} (lines 147-154) is a return value, not a call argument, as before; haiku-2's do: clauses for payload/2 (lines 107-111) are one expression each.

Probe of 28 payloads (the three known types, an unknown type, a non-string and a missing type, missing, nil, string and negative amount, missing and nil currency, missing customer_email and payment_id, payment.failed without and with an integer failure_reason, refunds missing refund_id or payment_id, a refund with a string amount, a string and an out-of-range created, missing created, missing and non-string id, missing and list data, a string and a nil payload), run in the scratch folder against each compiled file; nothing raises. In all four: the three known types parse; an unknown type gives {:unsupported_event, "invoice.paid"}; "type" => 123 gives {:unsupported_event, 123}; a known type without amount gives {:missing_field, "amount"}, not unsupported; a nil, string or negative amount gives {:invalid_field, "amount"}; a missing currency or payment_id names that field and a nil currency gives {:invalid_field, "currency"}; refunds without refund_id or payment_id name that field and a refund with a string amount parses (no Refund has an amount); a string or out-of-range created gives {:invalid_field, "created"}; payment.failed without failure_reason parses; a payload missing type, id, created or data, or a non-map payload, gives :invalid_payload. Differences: "id" => 5 and list data give {:invalid_field, "id"} and {:invalid_field, "data"} in haiku-2 and sonnet-2 and :invalid_payload in haiku-1 and sonnet-1; a missing customer_email is rejected by the Haiku runs and accepted by the Sonnet runs, whose Payment leaves it out of @enforce_keys; "failure_reason" => 5 is accepted only by haiku-2, which reads it with brackets and does not check it.

Compared with the previous skill sweep (2026-10-31-b at 74112b4, Haiku and Sonnet tiers only, since this batch has no opus run): Match every expected shape moves from Sonnet clean to violated (both Sonnet runs write the parse_data(_payment_type, ...) catch-all); Comments moves from Sonnet violated to clean (no wrong doctest; all doctests pass); the `->` rule moves from Haiku clean to violated (haiku-2's success row calling text/2), decided by the call-on sentence, which 2026-10-31-b did not have. The other seven rules stay clean in both tiers. Compared with 2026-11-05-check-3 at 9a47da2: Match every expected shape stays Sonnet violated (2 of 2 runs now, 1 of 2 there); Comments moves Sonnet violated to clean; the `->` rule moves Haiku clean to violated on the success-calls-on pair that 2026-11-05-check also counted in both Haiku runs. The rewritten `->` text changes no verdict that the check-3 wording would have given here; with two runs per tier the other moves are differences between runs.
